title: Germany tests IdentiFlight cameras for bird protection
summary: An OECD entry reports German deployment in September 2022. OekoFor's undated firsthand account describes German test-site validation, without a measured reduction in bird fatalities.
account: The OECD AI Incidents entry summarizes press coverage of 20 and 21 September 2022 (The Guardian, Mother Jones, The Register and others, not among the sources). It says that Germany is deploying AI-powered camera systems developed by IdentiFlight to detect endangered lesser spotted eagles near wind turbines and slow the blades to prevent collisions. The monitor's rationale cites the 82% reduction reported from the Wyoming study rather than a German measurement. OekoFor's undated page, also retained among the sources, describes IdentiFlight systems installed at German test sites. OekoFor and ARSU supervise validation that compares the systems' observations with ornithologists' reference data. The undated page does not establish when those tests began or supply a German fatality-reduction estimate.
purpose: IdentiFlight is built to detect eagles and curtail turbines; protecting lesser spotted eagles at German wind farms is the intended use.
system: IdentiFlight automated eagle detection and turbine curtailment

ratings.reason: No German fatality data are documented.
No operator or site outcome is documented.

ai_role.statement: The OECD registry reports deployment, while OekoFor's undated firsthand account confirms validation at German test sites. The inspected material does not measure IdentiFlight's effect on bird fatalities in Germany. The Wyoming effect estimate should not be transferred to the German tests.
